title: AI Fundamentals
description: This module introduces learners to the foundational concepts of artificial intelligence and machine learning, establishing the mental models needed before diving into security topics. Rooms cover AI/ML threat categories, how models consume and process data, prompt engineering basics, and how AI can be used to augment existing roles using digital forensics as an example with a companion challenge to close off.

title: Secure AI Systems
description: This module explores AI systems as an attack surface, covering secure architectural design principles and how to identify weaknesses at the system integration layer. Learners examine LLM-specific security concerns, apply threat modelling frameworks like STRIDE and OWASP in AI contexts, and practice attack surface discovery when AI components are present. The module concludes with a static site exercise where learners put their AI threat modelling skills to the test.

title: Prompt Security
description: This module covers one of the most prevalent AI attack classes: prompt injection. Learners begin with direct injection techniques before moving on to jailbreaking and instruction smuggling via external content. The module then shifts to the defensive side, covering hardening techniques including filters, guards, and template isolation. Two challenge rooms provide hands-on red experience, reinforcing both attack recognition and mitigation strategies.

title: AI Supply Chain Security
description: This module focuses on the security of AI models from procurement through deployment. Learners investigate how supply chains are targeted (OWASP LLM03), how to detect tampered or untrusted artefacts at ingestion, and how embedded triggers, poisoned checkpoints, and compromised fine-tunes manifest in real-world scenarios. Two hands-on challenge rooms reinforce defensive skills in identifying and responding to malicious models.

title: Data Poisoning
description: This module descends into the deepest layer of AI security: the data. Learners explore risks specific to Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, attacks targeting ingestion pipelines and embeddings, and how private data can be exposed through retrieval or embedding leakage. Mapped to OWASP LLM02, LLM04, and LLM08, the module closes with two scenario-based challenges centred on RAG poisoning detection and defence.

title: 2026: An AI Odyssey
description: Module containing all event rooms for the "2026: An AI Odyssey" CTF

title: Jr Pentester Challenges
description: This module is the capstone of the path. Four full-scope challenges put every skill you’ve built into action against environments designed to mirror real penetration tests, with no guided walkthroughs to lean on. You’ll move from reconnaissance through exploitation, privilege escalation, and lateral movement on your own, working through targets that get progressively more demanding as you go. Completing them proves you’re ready to operate at the junior pentester level.

title: Penetration Testing Foundations
description: This module drops you straight into the action with two guided engagements: one against a web application and one against a vulnerable machine. You’ll walk through each attack from reconnaissance to exploitation, see how the cyber kill chain structures attacker thinking, and meet the industry-standard frameworks that shape professional engagements. By the end, you’ll have the working mental model every penetration test relies on.

title: Network Reconnaissance
description: Reconnaissance is where every engagement begins, and this module covers both halves. You’ll start with passive techniques that mine public records, search engines, and DNS data without ever touching the target, then move into active probing with classic network utilities to map live systems. From there, you’ll work through the everyday protocols and services that keep networks running, learning how each one behaves and how attackers turn its quirks against it.

title: Web Application Security Fundamentals
description: This module opens your web application testing journey by teaching you to walk through a target the way an attacker does, surfacing the hidden pages, directories, and files that ordinary users never see. You’ll then dig into the modern stacks that power today’s sites, understanding how frontend frameworks, APIs, and backend technologies each introduce their own attack surface. By the end, you’ll be running practical web server attacks and reading them through a pentester’s lens.

title: Web Application Vulnerabilities I
description: This module walks you through five of the most impactful vulnerabilities in modern web applications, examining how each works, why it persists, and how attackers exploit it in the wild. You’ll start with the classics, SQL injection and cross-site scripting, before moving to subtler bugs like CSRF, SSRF, and IDOR that often slip past even experienced developers. A final hands-on challenge brings all the techniques together, so you finish the module able to spot these issues quickly and exploit them with confidence.

title: Web Application Vulnerabilities II
description: This module takes your web hacking beyond the classics into the vulnerabilities that turn small oversights into full-system compromises. You’ll begin with the mechanics of session management and authentication, then move on to server-side attacks such as directory traversal and command injection, and finish with the rapidly expanding attack surface of modern APIs. A live security challenge closes the module, so the techniques are battle-tested before you carry them into the rest of the path.

title: Vulnerability Knowledge
description: This module is about how penetration testers stay ahead of the curve, starting with the public vulnerability databases (CVE, NVD, vendor advisories) that catalog every known weakness in modern software. You’ll then move into the scanning tools that do the heavy lifting at scale, before picking up the manual identification techniques that turn raw scanner output into reliable, actionable findings. By the end, you’ll know how to research a CVE from first principles and validate whether it actually applies to a target.

title: Password Attacks
description: This module steps into the attacker’s playbook for stealing and cracking credentials, opening with phishing, the social engineering classic that still catches cautious users off guard. From there, you’ll run online attacks with Hydra, build custom wordlists tailored to a target, and use them to crack captured password hashes offline. A live password challenge closes the module, putting every technique into a realistic credential attack chain.

title: Metasploit and Exploitation
description: This module covers exploitation from two complementary angles: Metasploit, the framework that powers countless real-world engagements, and the manual craft that underpins it. You’ll work through Metasploit from the ground up, learning to scan for vulnerabilities, exploit live systems, run post-exploitation modules, and generate custom payloads with msfvenom. From there, you’ll move beyond the framework to build your own shells, listeners, and payloads from scratch, so you can weaponize an exploit whether a framework is on the table or not.

title: Active Directory Security Testing Basics
description: Active Directory sits at the heart of nearly every corporate network, which makes it one of the most valuable targets in any engagement. This module takes you behind the scenes, starting with how AD authentication actually works under the hood before walking through the full attack chain: breaching the domain, enumerating users and machines, harvesting credentials, and moving laterally to expand your foothold. Two live AD challenges close the module, so the full chain is something you’ve executed end to end.

title: Specialized Domains
description: This module branches out beyond the core pentesting path into the specialized domains shaping modern cyber security. You’ll explore wireless, mobile, and cloud security to see how each environment introduces its own attack surface, step into the rapidly emerging world of LLM pentesting, and shift perspective to see how defenders tackle the same problems through the blue team lens and DevSecOps practices. By the end, you’ll have a clear picture of where the field is going and which specialization might be right for you.

title: Python Scripting Basics
description: Python is the go-to scripting language for penetration testers and the engine behind countless security tools used in the wild, and this module takes you from zero to writing your own. You’ll start with a guided demo to get a feel for the language, move into core programming concepts (variables, control flow, functions, data structures), and build your first standalone scripts. The module finishes with scripts tailored to real pentesting work, so the language becomes a tool you can actually reach for on an engagement.

title: Pentesting Methodologies and Reporting
description: This module covers the professional workflow that turns hacking skills into a real engagement. You’ll start with threat modeling and scoping, the planning work that happens before a single tool runs, then move into writing clear, actionable pentest reports that communicate findings to both technical and non-technical audiences. The module closes with the re-testing process, which verifies remediations and signs an engagement off, leaving you with an end-to-end view of how professional pentests are actually delivered.

title: Privilege Escalation
description: This module is about turning a foothold into full control of a system. You’ll begin with host configuration reviews, learning to spot the misconfigurations that make privilege escalation possible in the first place, then dig into Linux privesc through manual enumeration, common vectors, and automated tooling. From there, you’ll cross into the very different world of Windows privilege escalation, before two live challenges put every technique into practice across both operating systems.

title: Incident Response Lifecycle
description: Incident response is not just a process on paper. In this module, you will work through a complete security incident at a company from start to finish, following the NIST incident response lifecycle across four rooms. Each room covers one phase of the lifecycle, building on the last, with every finding carrying forward into the next. By the end, you will have worked a real incident end to end the same way an IR analyst would on the job.

title: Welcome to AWS
description: AWS is one of the largest cloud providers, and understanding how it works is the first step to securing it. This module introduces you to the building blocks of AWS: how identities are created and managed, how networks are structured, how data is stored, and what tools AWS provides to defend it all. Whether you are new to cloud or coming from a different background, this module sets the stage for everything that follows.

title: Identity and Access Management
description: In AWS, who you are determines what you can do, making identity one of the most targeted attack surfaces. Misconfigured policies, forgotten access keys, and overly permissive roles are among the most exploited weaknesses in the wild. This module challenges you to find and fix real IAM misconfigurations, building the defensive instincts needed to protect the identities that control your cloud.

title: Network and Perimeter Defense
description: Network misconfigurations are a silent and persistent threat in AWS. An overly permissive security group, an unintended public subnet, or a forgotten access rule can be all an attacker needs. This module walks you through the layers of AWS network security, examining real misconfiguration scenarios, teaching you to spot what is wrong, and equipping you with the skills to lock down your environment before it is too late.

title: Securing Compute
description: Every running workload in AWS is a potential target. Exposed management interfaces, unpatched software, abused metadata services, and misconfigured containers are real threats that defenders encounter in production environments. This module takes you through hands-on scenarios built around common attack patterns, teaching you to harden your compute resources.

title: Storage and Data Security
description: Storage misconfigurations are among the most common causes of cloud data breaches and among the most preventable. From publicly accessible objects to snapshots shared beyond their intended audience, the risks are significant and the impact severe. This module explores how AWS storage services can be inadvertently exposed, teaches you how to spot them, and equips you with the controls needed to keep your data secure.

title: Web Frameworks
description: This module covers white-box web application testing: tracing a vulnerability from source code to a working exploit across the frameworks that carry most production traffic. Learners start with the review method itself, reading code, mapping attack surface, and grepping for dangerous patterns, before applying it stack by stack. Spring Boot brings Actuator misconfiguration, SQL injection below the ORM, mass assignment, and deserialisation. Django and Flask bring debug exposure, session forgery, and template injection. ASP.NET brings ViewState tampering, mass assignment, and deserialisation. Each framework room ends with a practical task chaining that stack's bugs into one exploit path, and a hard capstone challenge closes the module by combining four Spring Boot flaws in a single unredacted codebase to reach remote code execution.

title: Advanced Elastic
description: In this module, we will build an Elastic Stack from its components and use it for log collection, endpoint protection, and alerting. We would shift away from legacy ELK terminology and instead focus on modern features and best practices, including ECS, Elastic Agent, Elastic Defend, and more.

title: Detection Engineering for SOC
description: As a SOC analyst, you handle alerts daily, but where do they come from, and what gets missed? In this module, you'll build an engineering mindset, work through the detection lifecycle, and build atomic, stateful, correlation-based, and anomaly detections against a full attack chain in Elastic. You'll then learn Sigma for writing detection logic once and deploying it anywhere, and finish by scaling with Detection-as-Code and AI-assisted detection. These skills apply to any SOC, whatever SIEM you run.

title: Cyber Threat Intelligence
description: Attacks are getting faster and more complex, and exchanging intelligence with the other defenders has become essential for any security team to keep up. We'll cover core Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) concepts and see how CTI differs from simple reputation lookups. You'll then see how to apply CTI to alert triage and incident response, and work with open-source platforms like MISP and OpenCTI.

title: Wazuh for SOC and GRC
description: Learn how to leverage Wazuh to satisfy both SOC and GRC requirements. Explore Wazuh's core architecture, vulnerability detection, and compliance reporting before diving into detection engineering with custom alert rules and decoders. To complement Wazuh, the module introduces Osquery for deep system visibility during threat hunting.

title: SOC Level 2 Capstone Challenges
description: In this module, you will work with Splunk and Elastic to investigate breaches based on real-world incidents. You will also complete one on-host Linux analysis challenge and one threat intelligence challenge, covering the different duties an L2 analyst can have. Once finished, you should be well-prepared for the SAL2 certification. Good luck!

title: Threat Hunting
description: In this module, you will progress through threat hunting from fundamentals to hands-on investigation. Starting with core concepts and methodologies, you will learn to hunt known tactics and techniques using real data in a SIEM. The module builds progressively. Each room covers a different phase of an attack chain, from initial access through impact. By the end, you will have conducted threat hunts end-to-end and investigated real-world scenarios, preparing you to hunt threats proactively in your own infrastructure.

title: Static Malware Analysis
description: In this module, we will learn how to understand a malware's purpose and behavior just by looking at its metadata, properties, and actual code. We will explore the tools used to analyse binaries, scripts, and MS Office files, and practice on real-world malware examples.

title: Intro to SOC Level 2
description: With attacks growing more complex and routine work becoming automated, the skill bar for security analysts is rising. Throughout this module, you'll see what Level 2 analysts do, what knowledge they need, and why this role matters for any mature SOC.

title: Advanced Traffic Analysis
description: This module covers network traffic analysis in modern environments, where CDNs, QUIC, and encrypted DNS have changed what defenders can see on the wire. You will learn to spot visibility gaps and pick the right data source, write and tune Snort rules, monitor traffic with Zeek, hunt with Zui, and analyse packets in Wireshark and TShark. Through hands-on labs, you will investigate command and control, lateral movement, and data exfiltration across cleartext and encrypted channels.

title: First Shift
description: Revisit the First Shift CTF from winter 2026 through six hands-on challenges preparing you for the SOC role, starting from easy CTI, EDR, and phishing analysis challenges, and continuing to much harder network analysis and Splunk scenarios that will truly test your SOC skills and put you into a day in the life of a real analyst.

title: PT2 Preparation
description: This module is compiled as a final checkpoint before you sit the PT2 exam, built around the attack surfaces that separate a junior-level operator from an advanced one. You will break out of containers, execute payloads entirely in memory, and work around the detection controls that modern cloud environments depend on. The bulk of the module is a deep run-through of Active Directory at forest scale: trust theory first, then child domain escalation, PAM and cross-forest trust abuse, NTLM relay, and ADCS certificate template attacks. Along the way, you will pivot through SQL Server linked servers, exploit SSH misconfigurations for lateral movement, and use BloodHound to turn a pile of collected data into a shortest path to Domain Admin.

title: Agent Building
description: This module teaches a repeatable, methodology-first framework for building AI agents: Discovery, Design, Foundations, Building, Evaluation, and Hardening. All Using a single evolving case study, the Atlas Research Agent. Learners go from deciding whether an agent is worth building through to shipping a working, evaluated, and security-hardened agent mapped to the OWASP Agentic Top 10.

title: Repossessed
description: TryHatMe Studios is putting the finishing touches on NeuralNexus, its long-awaited platformer about a newly departed soul working through the afterlife's paperwork, one numbered ticket at a time. Launch is close, and the whole office has gone black-and-white stripes to celebrate.  This morning, something odd shows up in the SIEM: a Marketing workstation spawns a process it has no business spawning. Nothing has crashed, nothing looks obviously broken... but the process tree doesn't sit right.

title: Credential Access: T1003
description: Investigate a Credential Access technique involving T1003.002: Security Account Manager. A registry tool has been used to export sensitive credential hives from a TryHatMe Studios workstation. Your task is to investigate this activity and determine whether this credential access is benign or malicious.

title: Discovery: T1033
description: Investigate a Discovery technique involving T1033. A detection rule has triggered an alert on THM-LUKE. Your task is to investigate this event and determine whether this user discovery activity is benign or malicious.

title: Privilege Escalation: T1548
description: Investigate a Privilege Escalation technique involving T1548. A detection rule has triggered an alert on THM-LUKE. Your task is to investigate this event and determine whether this elevation activity is benign or malicious.

title: Execution: T1569
description: Investigate an Execution technique involving T1569.002: Service Execution. A detection rule triggered on a TryHatMe Studios workstation after an unusual service control manager operation was observed shortly after the user ran a downloaded utility. Your task is to investigate this event and determine whether this activity is benign or malicious.

title: Execution: T1047
description: Investigate an Execution technique involving T1047: Windows Management Instrumentation. A user at TryHatMe Studios downloaded and double-clicked a file on their workstation. An alert fired shortly after. Your task is to investigate this event and determine whether this execution activity is benign or malicious.

title: Execution: T1059
description: Investigate an Execution technique involving T1059. A detection rule triggered an alert on THM-LUKE. Your task is to investigate this event and determine whether this activity is benign or malicious.

title: Execution: T1204
description: Investigate an Execution technique involving T1204.002: User Execution: Malicious File. Your task is to investigate this event and determine whether this alert shows benign or malicious activity.

title: Persistence: T1543
description: A "T1543: New Service Installation Detected" rule triggered on THM-MKT-WS. Your task is to investigate this event and determine the nature of the detected activity.

title: Persistence: T1098
description: A T1098: User Added to Privileged Local Group rule triggered an alert on THM-IT-DESK. Your task is to investigate this event and determine the nature of the detected activity.

title: Persistence: T1197
description: A detection rule "T1197: BITS Service Spawning Suspicious Child Process" triggered an alert on THM-DEV-WS. Your task is to investigate this event and determine whether this alert shows benign or malicious activity.

title: Persistence: T1574
description: A "T1574.001: Unsigned DLL Loaded From Trusted Application Path" rule triggered an alert on THM-DEV-WS. Your task is to investigate this event and determine the nature of the detected activity.

title: Persistence: T1037
